facts.raw_span: painful swelling of the calves
no evidence of deep venous thrombosis or soft-tissue infection
elevated LDH and CK
negative autoimmune serology
CT scan showed no lymphoma relapse but diffuse subcutaneous edema
elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH
reduced plasma protein, albumin, and IgG
MRI of the thighs showed diffuse intramuscular and extramuscular edema
muscle biopsy demonstrated interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates
acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis
ECG revealed a new right bundle branch block and repolarization disturbances
CSF analysis showed leukocyte count 329/μl, lactate 3.5 mmol/L, and protein 79.6 mg/dl

concepts.why: Elevated CK and muscle biopsy with infiltrates suggest polymyositis
Elevated troponin and ECG changes indicate myocarditis
Acute kidney injury and elevated CK suggest rhabdomyolysis
CSF analysis and spinal MRI suggest acute myelitis
Elevated CRP and leukocytosis indicate a systemic inflammatory response
Elevated CK and muscle biopsy with infiltrates could suggest dermatomyositis, but skin involvement is not mentioned
Elevated CK and muscle biopsy with infiltrates could suggest inclusion body myositis, but characteristic features are not mentioned
Elevated troponin and ECG changes could suggest cardiac sarcoidosis, but granulomas are not mentioned

rationales.F01: Painful swelling of the calves is a common symptom of polymyositis.
rationales.F03: Elevated LDH and CK are indicative of muscle damage, which is consistent with polymyositis, myocarditis, and rhabdomyolysis.
rationales.F06: Elevated CRP, transaminases, CK, troponin I, myoglobin, and LDH are indicative of a systemic inflammatory response and muscle damage.
rationales.F09: Muscle biopsy demonstrating interstitial and perivascular T-cell and macrophage infiltrates is consistent with polymyositis.
rationales.F10: Acute kidney injury secondary to rhabdomyolysis is a complication of severe muscle damage.
rationales.F11: ECG changes and elevated troponin I are indicative of myocarditis.
rationales.F12: CSF analysis showing elevated leukocyte count, lactate, and protein is consistent with acute myelitis.
